title: Killer baseline
text: Killer baseline The creator's verdict after the September 14 near-full-lobby playtest was that the killers were too easy: running away always worked, because pursuit ran at 3.25 m/s against a 4.3 m/s player run. The September 15 pressure pass raises pursuit with the crew, adds a close lunge, makes worksite doors part of the chase and re-rolls field obstacles every stop. The sensing and search behaviour below is unchanged. These are accepted starting values, not measured balance. Sensing and search tuning Killer Walk hearing Run hearing Search budget Search points Groundskeeper 10 m 20 m 18 s 4 Rattletrap 14 m 26 m 22 s 5 Roadkill 8 m 18 m 14 s 3 Hitchhiker 8 m 16 m 12 s 3 Usher 9 m 18 m 18 s 4 Switchboard 10 m 22 m 20 s 4 Movement sensing uses horizontal player speed: greater than 0.6 m/s starts walking noise, greater than 3 m/s uses running range. Detection distance is spherical. Soft Soles multiplies movement ranges by 0.75. Safe, downed/ineligible, and suspended players are excluded. This does not inspect microphone input. Visible and audible candidates are distinct. Vision takes priority; sound behind cover starts investigation without granting sight-only warnings/attacks. New sound evidence refreshes at most every 0.8 seconds. When a player becomes quiet or leaves hearing range, the last evidence and deadline stop following them. Rattletrap remains blind, with the largest movement ranges and separate task-noise investigation. Usher investigates after a broken warning and must warn afresh when it visually reacquires. Turning corners and searching Observed movement can project a short continuation, bounded to five metres. Mode 6 searches alternate nearby reachable NavMesh probes with authored route anchors. Missing route anchors no longer cause instant abandonment. Searches have both time and point budgets, so the configured duration is a ceiling rather than a guaranteed wait. Search pauses sweep left/right for 2.2 seconds through a ±100° range. Moving patrol/search adds bounded lateral scanning (±28° patrol, ±45° search) without stopping navigation. Actual facing drives vision and presentation. Synced checkpoint fields preserve probe position, progress, reference heading, and sensing state. Speed, lunges and the cost of a hit Pursuit is a multiple of the players' base run speed and patrol a multiple of their base walk speed (2.7 / 4.3 m/s), and both rise linearly with the crew to +20% at eight or more participants. The crew count is the stop's locked count lowered by departures, so late joiners never speed a hunter up mid-stop. Killer Solo 4 crew 8+ crew Groundskeeper, Rattletrap, Usher, Switchboard 4.30 4.67 5.16 Roadkill (its charge is the threat) 4.09 4.44 4.90 Hitchhiker burst 4.73 5.14 5.68 Patrol is 2.70 m/s solo and 3.24 m/s at 8+, so an unaware hunter still reads as unhurried. Evidence younger than three seconds is run down at full pursuit pace; older evidence is searched at 85%. Pursuit no longer brakes toward the player's last position and aims at a bounded lead along their observed route. Inside three metres a hunter bursts to 130% for 0.6 seconds with a four-second cooldown. A landed hit costs the hunter a 1.5-second recovery, so two health cannot collapse into a single catch, and Roadkill's 9 m/s charge is unchanged. Players run 4.3 m/s, 5.16 on Sprint soda and 3.655 carrying cargo without Courier, so distance alone no longer escapes: cover, doors, the refuge and stuns do. Doors and per-stop layouts Worksite front openings have hinged doors. Crew open and close them; the owner validates distance, eligibility, a cooldown and whether anyone stands in the doorway or the leaf's swing. Doors deliberately do not carve navigation: a hunter stops at a closed leaf, opens it in 0.8 s when unhurried, and bashes it off its hinge in 1.2 s while pursuing or following fresh evidence — a broken door stays open for the rest of the stop, so a door buys distance once and cannot be looped. Rear openings stay clear as a second exit. Every stop attempt also rolls a fresh set of field obstacles (hay bales, stalled vehicles, log piles, crates, drums, a trailer). Solid parts carve the navigation mesh at runtime, and after each roll the owner verifies that all 114 authored patrol, cargo, repair and supply destinations remain reachable, re-rolling twice and then falling back to a clear field. The spectator map draws the active obstacles and closed doors over its baked terrain. Presentation and debug surfaces The world killer model and spectator map use the same always-active feed. Non-owners wait for a matching pose, snap on the first valid sample/round change, then interpolate nearby updates. Feed data includes warning/hazard/decoy state and hearing ranges. The map’s gold vision outline is clipped against cover; blue rings show walking/running hearing. The legend also reports the hunter's current speed and crew factor, and the map draws gray blocks for the rolled obstacles and cream bars for closed doors, so a watcher sees the same field the crew is in. Explicit sorting keeps them above terrain. Only eligible dispatch spectators can view tracking. The map is a horizontal projection, so vertical cover and actual head visibility can differ. Host → AI diagnostics is an optional independent reader for owner IDs, heartbeat age, path state, feed receipt, presentation readiness, and movement information. It now reports Killer v4 with the current speed, landed hits, lunges and doors opened or broken; the owner logs the same line on mode changes and every ten seconds. Mode 7 is “at a door”. Radar visibility and diagnostics are development features; decide whether to remove or restrict them before release. Deferred work and acceptance Fair search persistence and pressure distribution for solo through 16 participants. Human evasion across multiple corners, noisy work, decoys, and changing routes. Roadkill charge visibility versus actual hits under latency. Hitchhiker warp presentation and safe relocation tells. Switchboard hazard cover rules, warning/active distinction, and alternate escape routes. Unreachable targets with reachable alternatives and owner changes in every mode. Cooldown/stun immunity and strong-perk builds without unavoidable chains. Whether the new speeds are fair rather than merely hard. crewSpeedBonus and the per-killer chaseSpeedRatios are the first inspector values to lower if a chase reads as unavoidable. Door agreement across clients and after owner migration, and the stop-start navigation carve cost on Quest and iPhone. The local lanes cover navigation, frozen evidence, hearing boundaries/perks, search expiry, synced metadata, and rendered rings/cones. The fresh uploaded fairness and migration matrix remains open.

title: Environment & art direction
text: Environment & art direction The current worlds are functional grayboxes with original placeholder geometry and synthesized sounds. The next pass should make the trip worth playing repeatedly before investing in fine AI tuning. Campfire as a gameplay anchor The protective lantern and covered van refuge are the dependable destination in every stop. Make their warm silhouette readable from escape routes. Preserve generous access and standing room for the crew; do not turn the entrance into a narrow collision trap. The van body is currently solid and the protected play space is its covered exterior. A walkable interior is an art/layout decision still to make. Keep exterior capacity even if an interior is added. Two locations to develop Area Existing foundation Next design questions Camp Deadwood Cabin/shed/shelter shapes and wooded routes Which loops create a second escape option? Where can the van lantern be glimpsed? Which shelters allow readable corner searches? Last Chance Service Station Pumps, canopy/garage/store and vehicle cover How do open forecourt risk and close service corridors differ? Can every job be approached from more than one direction? Aim for roughly 15–25 seconds of travel from the van to ordinary work sites. This is a design target to measure, not a claim that every current route meets it. Compact solo routes should remain interesting; larger crews need additional useful work sites, not just more repeated walking. Per-stop layouts and doors Each area has a Randomized layout root. Its children are sites; each site's children are the mutually exclusive variants one stop can roll — hay rows, stacked bales, stalled vehicles, fallen pines, log stacks, crates and pallets, a tractor, oil drums, a jackknifed trailer, a collapsed sign, tire stacks. The seeded content is graybox: 11 sites with 29 variants across both areas . Replace their meshes freely and add sites of your own; any geometry works, with solid parts on layer 11. Per site, emptyWeight sets how often nothing appears, variantWeights follow child order, and a positive routeGroup keeps at least one site of that group clear so several blockers can cross one corridor without sealing it. Keep obstacles at least 1.2 m clear of anchors and patrol points and 3 m clear of the refuge — the validator enforces it. Worksite front openings carry a hinged door: a frame, a leaf that swings inward, and an interaction trigger. Keep the leaf a single solid collider under the hinge and the doorway at least 1.2 m wide; the killer's agent is 0.9 m across. Rear openings must stay clear — supply anchors sit in them, and a cabin whose only two exits could both close is a dead end. After any of this, run SpookCo → Apply gameplay scene additions , which adds carving obstacles, keeps the new geometry out of the navigation bake and the spectator map texture, rebuilds navigation when static geometry changed, and re-collects the layout. Then run Validate scene and rules , which fails on a site with no variants, a variant that would block an anchor or the refuge, a mis-wired door, and a doorway the baked mesh cannot pass through. Re-bake lighting after adding static geometry such as door frames. Objective and round design Make cargo destinations, repair states, shared supplies, and extraction unmistakable through shape and feedback, not color alone. Retain interrupted repair progress and a soloable path through every mandatory task. Give leaving the refuge a reason: visible jobs, optional supplies, and short risk/reward decisions. Measure the 20/150/30/10-second phase rhythm with real players before changing timers. Test whether three stops produce variety through placement and killer combinations rather than repetitive chores. Preserve at least two plausible responses to ordinary pursuit; avoid compulsory dead ends and unavoidable spawn attacks. Art sessions 1 — Van and campfire: distressed company paint, protective lantern, awning, broad access, warm safe silhouette. Preserve zone, arrival, interaction, and navigation transforms. 2 — Killer identities: six strong silhouettes on a shared modest rig foundation. Keep visual weapon reach consistent with the simulation. Current procedural limb animation expects named arms/boots; replace deliberately if adding Animator rigs. Preserve attack warnings and hazard readability. 3 — Environment and sound: a modular cabin/garage kit, canopy, low-poly trees, shared atlas, and clear objective props. Replace synthesized warnings and decoy clicks with short original sounds; add restrained ambience and fire. Check voice-chat intelligibility and phone speakers. Asset budgets and authoring guardrails Current recorded geometry is 64,686 triangles across all loaded meshes , which includes the graybox layout variants and door frames. Initial mobile targets are below 70 MB download and about 250,000 visible world triangles; these are provisional, not frame-rate evidence. Start with a shared 1024-pixel atlas and simple materials. Prefer baked lighting, few transparent layers, limited particles/rigs/physics, and pooled supplies. There are 24 authored supply anchors per area; preserve compact solo eligibility and distinct reachable locations. Do not move protected zones, objective anchors, supply anchors, killer spawn points, patrol routes, the sixteen van and dispatch spawn spots, or the briefing barrier and its glowing marker accidentally when replacing meshes. Structural changes require navigation/lighting rebakes, scene validation, and all three platform builds. Add authors/licenses to credits when importing outside assets.

title: Development status
text: Current project status Playable baseline accepted. Not a release candidate. The creator reports that the basic game works, killers now provide a useful baseline, and Pass Host plus AFK Claim Host have been tested. The next priority is game and environment design; fine AI tuning is deferred until those decisions are clearer. Three passes landed on September 15, all of them from the September 14 near-full-lobby playtest: the VR playtest fixes (trip resume, dark transit, upright cargo, selling, a reworked VR panel), the killer pressure pass (crew-scaled pursuit, a close lunge, interactive worksite doors, per-stop field obstacles), and the briefing van hold with spread spawn spots. Everything in them is locally checked and none of it has been played by more than one real client yet — the chase now has to be judged by people, not fixtures. These notes are unlisted, public documentation . They are not linked from the player navigation or public search index. Do not put credentials, private playtester details, or raw logs here. Development-only spectator radar and AI diagnostics may change or be removed. How to read the status Implemented means the code and scene contain the feature. Locally checked means editor/static/ClientSim evidence exists. User confirmed identifies a reported uploaded playtest. Open means unfinished work or missing acceptance. These labels are deliberately not interchangeable. System register System Current state Remaining acceptance / work Three-stop trip and phase flow Implemented; basic loop user confirmed. Returning to dispatch keeps the trip open and the next departure resumes that stop; host End trip starts fresh Full 1/2/4/8/12/16-player trips, pace measurements, and the End trip reward policy Two locations and campfire refuge Playable grayboxes Route design, atmosphere, readable silhouettes, van art/interior decision Cargo, repairs, quotas, late entry Implemented; local checks Real concurrent work, disconnects, scaling transitions Damage, rescue, all-down recovery Implemented; local checks; capture observed in uploaded play Group/solo fairness and interrupted recovery cases Six killers and navigation Working baseline user accepted; local regression checks. Pursuit is now a ratio of the players' own run speed, +20% at eight or more crew, with a close lunge and a pause after a landed hit Whether a chase reads as hard rather than unavoidable at 1–16 crew; pressure allocation; charge/warp/hazard presentation Per-stop layouts and interactive doors Implemented; local layout/door lane with reachability verification Two-client door agreement, owner migration mid-stop, obstacles never trapping a player, the stop-start carve cost on Quest and iPhone Briefing van hold and spread spawn spots Implemented; local barrier geometry, layer isolation and spawn-ranking checks Roomscale walking against the barrier in a headset, the VR shop pointer passing through it, and spot spread with 2–8 real crew Movement hearing and multi-point search Implemented; local hearing/replication/render checks Natural human evasion and different party sizes Spectator map and remote killer model Shared feed and fixes implemented; local receiver/render checks Fresh non-owner and migration matrix; final radar policy Inventory, shop, shared loot Implemented; local transaction checks. Selling the equipped consumable refunds 50% bought / 25% found Real-client collection/purchase/sale races and interrupted grants XP, survival milestones, ten perks Implemented; local rule checks Reward economy, early upgrade timing, 20+ hour progression target Persistence and session wallets Restore/save paths implemented Uploaded reconnect, A → B → A, crash/save boundaries Ready/Watch and Force Start Implemented; local integration checks Simultaneous ready/cancel/departure and late join matrix Pass Host and AFK Claim Host User confirmed in uploaded play Offer decline/expiry, Keep Hosting, claimant departure, phase matrix Simulation ownership recovery Implemented; local fixtures Real suspension/departure during every transaction and AI mode Desktop controls and accessibility Implemented; creator has tested desktop Full shortcut/rebind/menu-interruption acceptance VR wrist/floating controls Implemented; the September 15 panel pass places the floating panel once, auto-closes it, and hides buttons that duplicate native controls Physical VR, handedness, seated and avatar-scale testing Touch controls Implemented; iPhone tried Discoverability, layout, touch ergonomics and Android phone tests 18-person instance overflow Accepted requirement; not implemented Admission and spectator/participant capacity policy and tests Art, animation, sound, lighting Original placeholders; baked lighting exists Final asset pass, readable cues, ambience, mix and credits Platform builds PC, Android, iOS SDK bundles successful Matching final uploads and physical platform verification Performance Small baseline assets; structural counts recorded 30-minute 1/16-player frame-time and memory captures Contest/release Planned Final rules/credits review, RC and manual submission Baseline snapshot Game checkpoint: 9a52009 — Merge briefing hold and spread spawns with the killer pressure pass . Unity 2022.3.22f1 , VRChat SDK 3.10.5 , AI Navigation 1.1.5 . Do not upgrade the project to obtain Unity 6 tooling. The latest local run contains 1,519 passing assertions across structural scene validation and thirteen ClientSim lanes, each lane in its own fresh session on the merged tree that carries both September 15 passes together. That is useful regression evidence, not 1,519 real multiplayer scenarios. See testing and release gates for exact lanes, dates, build sizes, and limits. Design work comes next Play the new pressure with real crews before touching its numbers again. If a chase reads as unavoidable rather than hard, the crew speed bonus and the per-killer chase ratios are the first inspector values to lower. Establish the rhythm of a stop: safe planning, uncertain search, readable pursuit, escape, and a short breather. The briefing hold and the per-stop obstacle roll are first attempts at the planning and search halves of that. Redesign the two graybox layouts around that rhythm, especially solo routes and the approach to the refuge. Define the van/campfire and six killer silhouettes before investing in detailed props. Play the core objectives repeatedly with small and large groups before changing AI numbers again. Keep regression coverage and record every new uploaded test with build, devices, party size, and result. Detailed systems , AI , environment/art , roadmap , and publishing instructions are maintained separately.

title: Updating this site
text: Updating this site One normal project push The canonical website source lives at Docs/site/ in the main SpookCo repository. Edit the Markdown in Docs/site/content/ , commit it with the rest of the project, and push main . The Publish documentation GitHub Action builds and checks the site, then copies only the generated website into the separate kittynXR/spookco-docs repository. GitHub Pages serves that repository at spookco.kittyn.cat . There is an ignored local checkout at Docs/site-repo/ for inspecting the deployment repository. It is not a submodule and does not need to be committed from the game repo. Do not author content there: the next publish replaces generated pages. No Unity assets, client logs, player data, or game source are copied to the public docs repository. Editing map File or folder Purpose content/index.md Player landing-page copy content/guide/ Quick start, controls, equipment, progression, threats, FAQ content/internal/ Current status, systems, AI, art/design, roadmap, testing, publishing assets/site.css Shared responsive visual design assets/site.js Navigation/search enhancement assets/night-shift.svg Original decorative illustration, not a screenshot build.py Markdown rendering, templates, separate search indexes, sitemap check.py Broken links/anchors and public/internal separation checks requirements.txt Pinned Markdown dependency The existing engineering reports outside Docs/site/ remain project documentation. They are not blindly mirrored to the public site. Update the curated status/testing pages when a new result supersedes an older one. Label results as implemented, locally checked, user confirmed, or open; include the tested build and date when available. Preview locally From Docs/site/ , create a Python 3.12+ virtual environment, install requirements, then run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python build.py python check.py python -m http.server 8765 --directory _build --bind 127.0.0.1 Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ and /internal/ . The build output and local environment are ignored by Git. The Action uses the same build/check commands before publication. Publishing and credentials The publishing Action runs for changes under Docs/site/** or its workflow, and can be run manually. It has read-only access to the main repo and uses a dedicated SSH deploy key with write access only to the docs repository. The private key is stored in the main repo’s SPOOKCO_DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY Actions secret. Never put its contents into source, Markdown, or logs. SSH host verification uses GitHub’s pinned Ed25519 host key. The docs repository publishes generated files from main at the repository root, with a .nojekyll file and CNAME containing spookco.kittyn.cat . Each deployment records the source revision in build-info.json . A failed build/check stops before replacing the deployed site; pushes are normal fast-forward updates with no force push. If publication fails, inspect the main repo’s Action first, then the docs repo’s Pages build/deployment. Confirm the deploy key still exists and the custom domain points to GitHub Pages. Cloudflare proxy/certificate changes can affect HTTPS independently of a successful site build. Public versus internal Player pages, player navigation, the public search index, and sitemap contain no links to /internal/ . Internal pages have their own navigation/search and noindex, nofollow metadata. This is discoverability separation, not authentication . Someone with the URL can read or share the pages, and the generated docs repository is public. Do not publish secrets or sensitive operational details here. If actual private team documentation becomes necessary, put it behind authentication instead of relying on an unlisted path. Platform references Publishing follows GitHub’s Pages publishing-source documentation , custom-domain setup , and deploy-key documentation .

title: Roadmap & open decisions
text: Roadmap & open decisions The original two-week plan remains a delivery framework. The current implementation moved ahead of final content, but not all acceptance gates are closed. September 15 raised killer pressure, gave the map per-stop obstacles and interactive doors, and added the briefing van hold with spread spawn spots. What all of it needs now is play data, not another local pass. Next: make the stops distinct Review solo and group routes in both areas and the readability of safe refuge access. Define the van/campfire visual identity and decide whether the van needs a walkable interior. Improve objective feedback and meaningful scavenging decisions. Watch whether the ten-second briefing hold actually produces shared planning or just reads as a cage, and whether the spread spawn spots land people somewhere useful. Choose a cohesive palette, lighting mood, modular environment kit, and six killer silhouettes. Measure short-loop fun and pacing with ordinary players. Killers now match a running player and reach +20% at eight or more crew, with cover, doors and re-rolled field obstacles as the counterplay; tune from that play data rather than from another local pass. Then: finish integration and scale Implement the accepted 18-person instance overflow policy while keeping gameplay tuned for 1–16 participants. Complete actual concurrent loot/purchase/cargo tests and reconnect A → B → A testing. Exercise ready countdown races, late entry, withdrawal, and quota reductions. Extend host-control testing beyond the user-confirmed Pass Host/AFK claim path to departures, cancellation, and suspension. Verify VR wrist/floating inventory, touch ergonomics, desktop direct shortcuts, and all accessibility alternatives. Then: balance, content freeze, and profiling Tune rewards toward a meaningful upgrade around the first half-hour and 20+ hours to full perk capacity; neither timing is yet measured. Test all six killers with starter solo loadouts in both areas and with larger groups. Review charge/warp/hazard fairness, repeated stuns, and strong perk combinations. Complete art/audio, warning clarity, credits, dawn report polish, and the final status of spectator radar/AI diagnostics. Run 30-minute 1/16-player performance sessions, report world and public-avatar costs separately, and fix measured bottlenecks. Release targets The working plan targets a September 27, 2026 release candidate with a buffer before the planned October 1, 2026, 11:59:59 p.m. Pacific submission deadline. These are planning dates. Recheck the official contest rules, content requirements, and submission instructions before release; this site is not an eligibility ruling. Produce matching PC, Android, and iOS builds, review SDK warnings and credits, upload manually, and submit manually. Do not equate successful asset-bundle compilation with a released world or contest submission. Decisions still open Decision Why it matters 18-person overflow behavior Creator exceptions can exceed a 16-person instance cap; runtime admission still needs handling. Final spectator information Full sensing radar may undermine mystery; current display is useful for testing. Debug controls in release Determine whether to strip, gate, or retain diagnostics. Van interior versus exterior refuge Changes art effort, collision, capacity, and navigation. Solo/group pressure and economy Current numbers are initial tuning; measure fun and progression. The accepted chase values (player run speed solo, +20% at 8+, a 130% lunge inside 3 m, a 1.5 s pause after a landed hit) are unmeasured against human evasion. End trip reward policy End trip deliberately ships unguarded for testing: play stop 1, return to dispatch, End trip, depart again, and that stop's objective, contract, extraction and rescue rewards pay again with freshly rolled supplies. The per-stop rate resembles a full run, so the gain is skipping stops 2–3 and the trip bonus rather than a rate exploit. Options: carry the ended trip's paid and claim masks forward for visited stops, put a cooldown on End trip, or accept it. Decide before release, and do not read progression pacing from sessions that used it. Briefing hold strength It is a courtesy constraint with no authority: a station, playspace drift or a modified client bypasses it, and roomscale walking against the barrier is still untested in a headset. Decide whether that is enough or whether the briefing needs a real gate. Final art/audio scope Keep two areas and six identities achievable without increasing mobile cost excessively.

title: Systems & architecture
text: Systems & architecture The game-host role and simulation ownership are independent. Passing Host changes who can operate the lobby/round controls; the simulation owner keeps advancing gameplay without waiting for host input. Runtime boundaries Component Responsibility SpookRules Stable catalogue IDs, tuning, XP curve, pouch packing, quota and movement rules SpookSession Phases, deadlines, crew state, host offers/claims, health/recovery, trip choices, authored spawn-spot selection, and the local briefing van hold SpookLedger Inventory/shop transactions, loot manifests and claims, rewards, cooldowns SpookProfile Restoration gate, permanent profile, bounded session wallets, accepted revision saves SpookObjectives Cargo reservation/carry/delivery, retained repairs, rescue work SpookKiller One native NavMesh agent, sensing, evidence/search, crew-scaled pursuit, attacks, durable AI checkpoint SpookLayout Per-stop obstacle rolls with reachability verification, and synchronized interactive door state SpookMapFeed Always-active shared killer/crew tracking and remote presentation snapshot SpookSpectatorMap Local spectator map, vision/hearing presentation and tracking age SpookControls Unified action routing, input priorities, saved device profiles SpookLoot At most 12 pooled shared supply objects; no per-pickup Update SpookPanel / SpookFeedback Throttled UI, markers, interaction targets, alerts, and the leased briefing barrier and its marker SpookTransition Local fade/teleport sequencing, replacement of obsolete destinations, and the leased black transit hold Authority and transactions Network entry points validate the actual caller, eligibility, and relevant revisions. A local click never grants an item. The ledger owner commits pouch changes and the shared claim in one synchronized object, with claimant/grant identity and duplicate protection. Full capacity rejects collection without claiming the pickup. Loot is rolled once per trip/stop. Restart Current Stop reuses the area, killer, manifest, and claims, but starts a clean objective attempt. Return to Dispatch keeps the trip open and records resumeStop , so the next departure resumes at that stop (or the next one if the stop was finished). Only the stop 3 report and the host's End Trip (phases 0–1) close a trip; the next departure after that is a fresh trip with new rolls. Every stop start bumps attemptSerial and clears that stop's field progress, while the once-per-trip objective and result reward masks prevent repeated payouts. Once-per-stop abilities and equipment cooldowns are also preserved. Transit between stops no longer teleports to the old van. Crew stay behind a black hold with locomotion paused, leased every session tick while phase 5 lasts plus a 5-second grace and a 20-second cap. The stop-start teleport runs under black and fades in over one second. Opening menus is refused during the hold. Selling the equipped consumable is a ledger transaction allowed in the same windows as buying. Bought supplies refund 50% and scavenged (found) supplies 25%; pouch bits 9–11 carry the per-slot found flag. The layout authority follows the simulation owner. Each stop attempt rolls one variant (or nothing) per authored site and an open/closed state per door, then verifies that every authored destination in the area is still reachable once the obstacles have carved navigation; it re-rolls twice before falling back to a clear field. Door toggles are owner-validated requests — able crew, within reach, in a running stop, not broken, past a cooldown, and with nobody in the doorway or the leaf's swing. An attempt first seen mid-stop adopts a clear field rather than dropping obstacles around players. Initial quotas and loot counts use the participating-player snapshot. Joins do not increase active quotas or supplies. Departures, withdrawal, and sustained suspension may lower outstanding requirements without erasing finished work. If nobody remains active, return to the lobby without completion rewards. Briefing hold and spawn placement For the first briefingSeconds - briefingLockSeconds (20 − 10) seconds of a briefing, each client keeps its own alive crew member inside the van area. Four local invisible walls on user layer 22 sit .5 m inside the refuge zone edge, enclosing the van, the operations panel and every spawn spot, with a glowing non-static marker while locked. This is a courtesy constraint, never authority. Nothing about it is synchronized, nothing scores on it, and a modified client, a station, playspace drift or VRChat's own respawn can bypass it. It fails open on every uncertain input: the wrong phase, a player who is not alive crew, a missing slot, missing rules, a missing safe zone, a halted session, and a deadline that is already past or more than briefingSeconds + 2 away — that last case releases silently, with no barrier, no countdown and no "Head out" notice, because the data cannot be trusted. A 1.5-second lease renewed by SpookSession and checked by SpookFeedback drops the walls if the session stops ticking. Layer 22 rather than Ignore Raycast: VRChat and ClientSim treat layer 2 as interactable, so a layer-2 wall would block the VR panel pointer whenever a pinned panel landed beyond it. The scene descriptor's Interact Passthrough includes layer 22, so interaction rays pass through while player movement still collides, and no gameplay query uses the layer — killer sight, cargo seating, the spectator map bake and the navmesh all use layer 11. Layer 22 does collide with the Pickup layer, so a carried or dropped case bumps the walls and stays inside the refuge for the ten seconds they stand. Walls arm only when the player is at least briefingArmInset (.85 m) inside the zone edge with no travel fade running, and stay armed while at least briefingKeepInset (.55 m) inside; a player pressed against a wall is .7 m inside, so a single threshold would disarm the barrier exactly when it is needed. A player outside the refuge while locked is teleported once to their own spot. The .35 s grace is sampled on the session's .2 s tick, so the effective pull-back delay is .4–.6 s. It is a direct teleport rather than a travel fade, so an open shop or loadout panel is not force-closed and the trip's teleport accounting is unchanged. Game-driven moves no longer stack the crew on one point. Sixteen authored, ground-seated spots sit under each van anchor and sixteen at dispatch, 1.5 m apart, clear of solid geometry, inside the barrier ring and facing the anchor's direction. They are used by transit arrival, stop start, restart, resume, late join, manual respawn at the refuge, recovery return, Watch, return to dispatch and the report. The local spot index is the player's rank by ledger slot — among crew for a van, among registered players for dispatch — where rank 0 keeps the original anchor, so solo positions are unchanged, and higher ranks map into spots 1–15 without ever wrapping back onto the anchor. Missing spot data falls back to the anchor, and VRChat's own join spawn still uses the single descriptor spawn. Three overlaps are accepted: more than 16 eligible players re-using spots 1–15, a spectator respawning at the plain refuge anchor, and a late joiner landing on a spot a teammate still occupies. Persistence Wait for OnPlayerRestored before writes, purchases, and grants. The permanent profile holds XP, survival points, perk selection, reusable gear, and player identity token. Separate VR/desktop/touch keys hold controls. A synchronized random live-session key survives trips, resets, role changes, and ordinary ownership migration. A bounded 128-record history stores session cash, pouch, cooldowns, inventory revisions, grant identity, and reward masks. The current wallet is updated during play; the history index changes only on session entry/eviction. Old prototype wallet data has a migration path. The implemented goal is same-session rejoin and A → B → A restoration without duplicated loot or refunded consumption. Actual cloud timing, interrupted writes, and concurrent-client race behavior remain uploaded acceptance work. No departure callback can guarantee a final cloud write after an abrupt crash. Stable content IDs Areas: 0 Camp Deadwood, 1 Last Chance Service Station. Killers: 0 Groundskeeper, 1 Rattletrap, 2 Roadkill, 3 Hitchhiker, 4 Usher, 5 Switchboard. Consumables: 0 empty, 1 ration, 2 soda, 3 flare, 4 tape. Reusable gear: 0 decoy, 1 camera, 2 EMF pager, 3 track shoes. Perk bits: Spotter, Courier, Mechanic, Field Medic, Scrapper, Soft Soles, Adrenaline, Quickdraw, Hardhat, Second Wind. Preserve IDs when replacing art or changing display names. Three consumable slots use three bits each and allow duplicates. XP to the next level is 150 + 35 × (current level − 1) through level 40; 31,785 total XP. Final reward pacing has not been measured. Capacity and transport limits Runtime admission is still 16 despite several storage/feed arrays having 32 slots. The accepted 18-person overflow requirement is not complete just because arrays are larger . Define admission, participants, and spectators explicitly before changing the cap. The AI checkpoint and presentation stream are separate. The always-active manual feed requests updates at 4 Hz; matching trip/stop/area/revision is required. A new owner can recover from a fresher presentation pose under a recovery interval. Local decoding/interpolation tests do not prove Photon delivery or suspension recovery.

title: Testing & release gates
text: Testing & release gates Evidence cutoff: September 15, 2026 Pacific (timestamps below use UTC). Every lane was rerun on the merged tree that carries both September 15 passes — killer pressure with per-stop layouts and doors, and the briefing van hold with spread spawns — one fresh ClientSim session per lane. Each pass also passed separately beforehand. The platform bundle table below is older than the lanes; see its own note. Human reports The creator reports that the basic loop works and the current killers are a useful baseline. Pass Host and AFK timeout / Claim Host have been tested in uploaded play. Desktop and iPhone have been tried. Earlier reports drove fixes for stalled pursuit, non-owner registration/tracking, desktop pointer/menu behavior, and sensing-outline visibility. These reports do not close every killer, device, and networking case. The held-W issue was attributed by the creator to the KVM setup and does not occur with the physical keyboard; no game-side keyboard workaround is required for that report. Latest local lanes Lane Started UTC Passing assertions Scene/rules validation 2026-09-16 00:09:47 554 Local gameplay 2026-09-16 00:10:46 68 Extended local integration 2026-09-16 00:12:18 220 Menu and travel presentation 2026-09-16 00:15:16 76 Killer pressure, layouts, doors 2026-09-16 00:15:48 79 Killer movement watchdog 2026-09-16 00:17:30 13 Warning-to-pursuit 2026-09-16 00:19:32 4 Crew registration 2026-09-16 00:20:13 23 Movement hearing / search 2026-09-16 00:20:40 99 AI review / diagnostics 2026-09-16 00:22:17 37 Corner pursuit 2026-09-16 00:24:19 12 Spectator map / negative clock 2026-09-16 00:24:56 143 Non-owner tracking receiver 2026-09-16 00:25:23 104 Killer replica/movement 2026-09-16 00:25:44 87 1,519 assertions across structural scene validation and thirteen ClientSim lanes, every lane passing. Structural checks, explicit SDK delegates, and single-VM ClientSim fixtures cover actual Udon paths where possible. Receiver decoding tests and rendering tests are useful but are not real Photon transport, cloud restoration, or physical input proof. The scene lane reports 64,686 triangles across all loaded world meshes , three non-directional lightmaps, 197/197 static renderers with baked lightmap indices , and 693 Udon behaviours including static UI handlers, the layout authority with its eight doors, and the editor-only validation fixture. None of those counts establishes Udon CPU cost or frame rate. It also covers the spawn-spot layout (anchor identity, offsets, ground seating, capsule clearance, spacing and refuge containment), the briefing barrier structure with its layer-22 collision row and the descriptor's Interact Passthrough bit, every collected layout site and door, obstacles keeping clear of anchors and the refuge, and baked navigation running through each doorway while its frame stays solid. The pressure lane measures patrol and pursuit speeds for all six killers at crew 1 and crew 8 through the real owner loop, the lunge and its cooldown, the recovery after a landed hit, crew and killer door handling with their refusals, eight layout rolls with reachability verification and a clear-field fallback, runtime navigation carving, and the spectator map's obstacle and door markers. The extended lane adds the briefing hold: arming with hysteresis, the escape grace and a single direct-teleport pull-back, shopping while held, the ten-second unlock, re-locking after a restart, a silent release on an implausible deadline, the lease shutdown on a halted session, watcher and late-join exemptions, and the barrier staying invisible to killer sight, cargo seating and the interact mask. It drove a held player into a wall through ClientSim's own character controller and the wall stopped them — that is evidence, not proof, and roomscale walking still needs a headset. Raw logs remain local/ignored; this public site publishes summaries only. Successful SDK bundles Platform Bytes Written UTC PC 2,923,464 2026-09-15 23:28:34 Android / Quest 2,310,266 2026-09-14 02:46:23 iOS 2,248,548 2026-09-14 02:48:28 The PC bundle was rebuilt after the killer pressure, layout and door pass, which also confirms the SDK accepts their carving navigation obstacles and bake-exclusion markers in a world build; it is smaller than the September 14 bundle because the non-directional lightmap fix and the geometry changes both affect it. It predates the briefing-hold pass, and the Android and iOS bundles predate both September 15 passes. These are VRChat world asset bundles, not standalone executables or exact client download/memory measurements. Reviewed non-blocking warnings include the mobile quality profile allowing multiple pixel lights (authored lights are baked), and an inapplicable iPhone C++ compiler option for this bundle workflow. Profile actual mobile lighting rather than dismissing the warning permanently. Uploaded test matrix still needed Complete normal trips with 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, and 16 participants; every killer, both areas, starter solo loadout. Ready/unready cancellation, Force Start, simultaneous departure, late entry, and 8 → 2 / 2 → 1 / 1 → 8 scaling without raised quotas or rerolled loot. Solo/all-down recovery, rescues, interrupted repairs, Second Wind, and safe refuge behavior. Several clients claiming one supply; full pouch; concurrent purchases; duplicate requests/grants; accessible and native cargo contention. Rejoin after earning, purchasing, scavenging, swapping, consuming, and using cooldowns; A → B → A; crashes during grants/saves. Host offer expiry/decline, Keep Hosting, meaningful activity cancellation, claimant/host departure, and ownership suspension in every phase. Non-owner map/model agreement, late snapshots, owner migration during charge/warp/stun, and effects/hits under latency. Chase balance at 1, 2, 4, 8 and a full lobby for every killer: whether distance alone still escapes, whether cover, doors and the van read as the answers, and whether any chase feels unavoidable rather than merely hard. Interactive doors with at least two clients: opening and closing from both sides, the refusal cases, a door slammed in a pursuing hunter's face breaking for the rest of the stop, agreement for late joiners and after owner migration, and nobody pushed or trapped by a swinging leaf. Per-stop layouts: obstacles differ between stops, never block an anchor or trap a player, the hunter paths around them, and a spectator sees the same field as the crew. Every direct/button alternative, both hands/wrists, seated/scale differences, menu interruptions, rebinding, profile persistence, and no unintended consumption or cargo drops. The VR panel pass: floating mode level and not in the face, tab switching never moving it, the three-metre auto-close, the launcher below the wrist staying clear of Close, Recenter, auto-close on expedition start, cargo grab and a hit, and glance status with alerts still visible. The briefing hold in a headset with 2–8 crew: roomscale leaning and walking into the barrier, jumping from the van roof, at most one snap-back with an open shop panel surviving it, the shop pointer passing through the wall, readable countdown and Head out text on every device, spectators and downed crew never held, a restart re-locking, and a stalled or implausible deadline releasing quietly. Spread spawns with real crews: no two players on one spot at departure or arrival, spots facing the van, and only the accepted overlaps (over 16 eligible players, a spectator at the plain anchor, a late joiner on an occupied spot). Trip resume: return to dispatch mid-stop and depart again, expecting a full attempt with no pre-done objectives and no second payout; End trip only at dispatch or during the countdown. End trip reward replay ships deliberately unguarded for testing, so progression pacing must not be read from sessions that used it. Hardware and performance Available: Linux PCVR with RTX 3090; Windows AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700; Quest 3; iPhone 16 Pro. Other testers can cover standalone Android phones. Confirm the exact PC headset and refresh rate when scheduling performance acceptance. Run 30-minute sessions with one and sixteen controlled lightweight avatars. Targets: PCVR 90 FPS, Quest 3 72 FPS, iPhone 16 Pro 60 FPS . Capture CPU/Udon and GPU frame time, batches, memory, textures/lightmaps, and bundle/download cost. Report public-avatar overhead separately. No current count or build result certifies these targets. Local commands Use the existing Unity editor and fixed-command bridge; do not launch a second editor for the same project. Tools/SpookCo.ps1 exposes status , refresh , reload-scene , compile , validate , patch-scene , clientsim , stop , smoke , extended , presentation , pressure , movement , pursuit , ai-review , corners , hearing , map-clock , remote-map , registration , replica , probe , bake , capture commands, and the platform build commands. Use a fresh ClientSim run per test lane. An asynchronous command acknowledgment is not completion: require a fresh result log ending in SUCCESS. Do not modify scripts during a build/test. World uploads and contest submission remain manual.
